name: [GSF2000] NGC 3627 C36
description: A Cepheid in the galaxy M66 that pulsates every 53.1 days.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 53.08 d in Gibson et al. (2000), ApJ 529, 723, VizieR J/ApJ/529/723/appen Cluster = NGC 3627, CNN = C36 (Per); not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 53.08 d in Gibson et al. (2000), ApJ 529, 723, VizieR J/ApJ/529/723/appen Cluster = NGC 3627, CNN = C36 (Per); not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of M66, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2022ApJS..261...21Y; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in M66 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 10,310,408 pc (src/objects/m66-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 10,313,356 pc, inclination 57.3 deg, line of nodes 173.1 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Tully et al. (2023), Cosmicflows-4, ApJ 944, 94; CDS J/ApJ/944/94, table 2 (distances of individual galaxies), PGC 34695: distance modulus 30.067 ± 0.061 mag (https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/cat/J/ApJ/944/94)

position.credit: Gibson et al. (2000), ApJ 529, 723, VizieR J/ApJ/529/723/appen Cluster = NGC 3627, CNN = C36 (Chip 4, Xpos 135.7, Ypos 125.4); the table names no exposure for this galaxy, so the pixel is read on the first exposure of its programme (GO 6549), u35i0101r, whose header places a pixel where those of four later epochs do

text.card: A Cepheid in the galaxy M66, 10.3 million parsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 53.1 days.
text.introduction: Gibson et al. (2000) list its pulsation at 53.1 days.
text.locator: VizieR J/ApJ/529/723/appen Cluster = NGC 3627, CNN = C36: Per

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M66 is not measured
